title: Learning keyboard slowly
summary: A note on learning keyboard without trying to turn it into another optimized project.
description: A note on learning keyboard without trying to turn it into another optimized project.
html:
I am learning keyboard slowly, which is probably the right way to learn it.

It is one of the few things in my life that I do not want to optimize too aggressively. Progress is uneven, mistakes are obvious, and that is part of the appeal.

There is something useful about working on a skill that does not care about dashboards, productivity language, or short-term output.

title: Living and studying in Germany
summary: A small reflection on how daily life in Germany has changed my pace and attention.
description: A small reflection on how daily life in Germany has changed my pace and attention.
html:
Living in Germany has changed the rhythm of my days more than I expected. Some of it is practical: public transport, university routines, paperwork, and the slow but steady work of learning the language.

Some of it is quieter. I walk more. I notice neighborhoods more. I have become more aware of the difference between being busy and paying attention.

That slower pace has been useful for study as well. Research usually benefits from patience more than urgency.

title: Organizing photos and memories
summary: Why I like keeping a lightweight photo archive instead of letting images disappear into storage.
description: Why I like keeping a lightweight photo archive instead of letting images disappear into storage.
html:
Most photos are easy to take and easy to forget.

I like the idea of keeping a lightweight archive where images have titles, dates, and a little context. It makes them feel less disposable and more like part of a lived record.

The goal is not perfect documentation. It is just enough structure to make a memory easier to revisit later.

title: Walking and cycling around Nürnberg
summary: A short note on using the city as a way to reset attention.
description: A short note on using the city as a way to reset attention.
html:
Some of my favorite parts of Nürnberg are not the headline landmarks but the routes between places.

Cycling or walking through the city is a good way to step out of problem-solving mode for a while. It clears the head without feeling like a formal break.

I like keeping small visual records of those routes. They help memory stay attached to place.

title: Why this page exists
summary: A short note about why I keep a personal page beside the professional portfolio.
description: A short note about why I keep a personal page beside the professional portfolio.
html:
Not everything belongs on a CV. Some things are better kept as thoughts: places, habits, experiments, and moments that explain the person behind the work.

I wanted this site to feel like a long-term archive, not just a hiring document. The professional side matters, but so do the quieter details that shape how I think and work.

That is what the personal page is for. It gives the site a second register: less polished, more observational, and easier to keep alive over time.
